1) the gastric mucosa contains many different proteins that continue to be synthesized for a long time in isolated gastric mucosal (IGM) cells; 2) the proteins that continue to accumulate in IGM cells have a wide range of relative specific radioactivities (RSRs), which is a measure of the extent of incorporation of radioactivity; 3) the RSRs are not related to the molecular weight or the staining intensity of the proteins.

The relative specific radioactivities (RSRs) of radiolabeled proteins synthesized in vitro by isolated gastric mucosa cells are determined by a computer program that identifies Gaussian components that contribute overlapping peaks in densitometric scans of stained gels (SDS gels), or of fluorographic film (FF) of radiolabeling experiments."

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the computer programs have enabled us to identify, with a high degree of precision, the relative specific radioactivities and the molecular sizes of proteins synthesized by isolated rat gastric mucosal cells and, in addition, to resolve overlapping bands of proteins in the range 15000 to 100000.

the computer programs described here provide a rapid and reliable method for the resolution of overlapping bands of protein and the determination of their relative specific radioactivities, and are applicable to the study of protein synthesis by isolated gastric mucosa and other cell types.
the computer programs have been developed to provide a method for the rapid and accurate resolution and quantification of the radioactivity in the protein bands of a polyacrylamde gel.
